items.title: Parabolic Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials for S_3 modulo S_2
items.statement: Take $W=S_3$ with simple reflections $s_1,s_2$, let $J=\{s_1\}$, so $W_J=\{1,s_1\}$ and the minimal left coset representatives are ${^JW}=\{e,\ s_2,\ s_2s_1\}$. In the notation of [[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] the two parabolic families are computed from the ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ (all ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of comparable pairs in $S_3$ equal $1$): the **antispherical (sign)** coefficients are $$n_{e,e}=1,\quad n_{e,s_2}=v,\quad n_{e,s_2s_1}=0,\quad n_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero; the **spherical** coefficients are $$m_{e,e}=1,\quad m_{e,s_2}=v,\quad m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2},\quad m_{s_2,s_2}=1,\quad m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v,\quad m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=1,$$ all other coefficients being zero. At $v=1$ the antispherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ and the spherical matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$. The two families therefore already differ for this smallest nontrivial parabolic: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=0$ while $m_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$.
items.strategy: Finite computation inside $H_v(3)$. The ordinary Kazhdan-Lusztig coefficients of $S_3$ are known from [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]] and the fact that all ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials of $S_3$ equal $1$: $p_{y,x}=v^{\ell(x)-\ell(y)}$ for $y\le x$ and zero otherwise, so the only nonzero values needed are $p_{e,e}=1$, $p_{e,s_1}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, $p_{e,s_1s_2}=p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$, $p_{e,w_0}=v^{3}$, $p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_2,s_1s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}=v$, $p_{s_2,w_0}=v^{2}$, $p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=p_{s_2s_1,w_0}=v$, and the diagonal ones $1$. The antispherical coefficients are the alternating sums $n_{y,x}=\sum_{z\in W_J}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{zy,x}$ of [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]. For $y=e$: $n_{e,e}=p_{e,e}=1$, $n_{e,s_2}=p_{e,s_2}=v$, and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v\cdot v=0$. For $y=s_2$: $n_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_2,s_2}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2}=1$ (the second term vanishes since $\ell(s_1s_2)>\ell(s_2)$), and $n_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1s_2,s_2s_1}=v-0=v$, the second term vanishing because $s_1s_2$ and $s_2s_1$ are distinct of equal length. For $y=s_2s_1$: $n_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{w_0,s_2s_1}=1-0=1$, the second term vanishing by the support condition. The spherical coefficients are $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$ ([[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]): $m_{e,e}=p_{s_1,s_1}=1$, $m_{e,s_2}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2}=v$, $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$, $m_{s_2,s_2}=p_{s_1s_2,s_1s_2}=1$, $m_{s_2,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1s_2,w_0}=v$, $m_{s_2s_1,s_2s_1}=p_{w_0,w_0}=1$. All arithmetic is in $\mathbb Z[v]$ with the Bruhat comparabilities of $S_3$ ([[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]], [[def-bruhat-order-on-the-symmetric-group]]); the coset set is ${^JW}=\{e,s_2,s_2s_1\}$ ([[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]]). An independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$, from the bar involution and the induced-module standard bases, reproduces both tables.

items.title: Spherical and antispherical normalizations give different polynomials
items.statement:
**Refuted claim:** the spherical and antispherical parabolic
Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients of
[[def-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis-and-polynomials]] agree (equivalently,
either normalization may be substituted for the other in a parabolic or
singular-block multiplicity statement).

The witness is the smallest nontrivial parabolic: $W=S_3$,
$J=\{s_1\}$, $W_J=\{1,s_1\}$, ${}^JW=\{e,s_2,s_2s_1\}$, where

$$n_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0\neq m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}.$$

At $v=1$ the antispherical value is $0$ while the spherical value is $1$, so
the antispherical number is not a unit multiple of the spherical one; as
polynomials they differ as well, so the discrepancy is not an artifact of
specializing at $v=1$.
items.strategy: Two-term computation in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$, using the ordinary Kazhdan--Lusztig coefficients $p_{r,s}=v^{\ell(s)-\ell(r)}$ for comparable pairs and zero otherwise. Antispherical: $n_{e,s_2s_1}=\sum_{z\in\{1,s_1\}}(-1)^{\ell(z)}v^{\ell(z)}p_{z,s_2s_1}=p_{e,s_2s_1}-v\,p_{s_1,s_2s_1}$ by [[thm-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-polynomials-are-alternating-sums-of-ordinary-ones]]; here $p_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}$ and $s_1\le s_2s_1$ with length gap one, so $p_{s_1,s_2s_1}=v$ and $n_{e,s_2s_1}=v^{2}-v^{2}=0$. Spherical: $m_{e,s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,s_1s_2s_1}=p_{s_1,w_0}=v^{2}$ by the reduction $m_{y,x}=p_{w_0^Jy,w_0^Jx}$ with $w_0^J=s_1$. The coset set and Bruhat relations are those of [[def-cg-parabolic-quotient-and-two-sided-minima]] and [[lem-bruhat-order-basic-properties-for-permutations]]; the values were checked by an independent construction of the two canonical bases in the normalized Hecke algebra of $S_3$ via the triangular construction of [[thm-existence-and-uniqueness-of-the-parabolic-kazhdan-lusztig-basis]]. The conclusion is a counterexample to any normalization-blind statement of the parabolic multiplicity theorem, not to the theorems themselves.

items.title: Translation to a singular wall in type A_2
items.statement:
Let $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and use the coordinate
$l=\langle\lambda,\alpha^\vee\rangle$, so the dot action is $s\cdot l=-l-2$
and the facets are $(-\infty,-1)$, $\{-1\}$, $(-1,\infty)$
([[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]], Example 3.11 of
the source). Take $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=-1$. Then the singular block
$\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)=M(-1)=P(-1)$, and the
translation functor $T=T_{-2}^{-1}$ satisfies $TM(-2)=M(-1)$, $TM(0)=M(-1)$,
$$TL(-2)=L(-1)\quad(\text{the label }1\in W^J),\qquad TL(0)=0\quad(\text{the label }s\notin W^J),$$
and $TP(-2)=2\,P(-1)$, because the projective cover $P(-2)$ of $L(-2)$ has
the Verma flag $\Delta(-2),\Delta(0)$ and both factors are sent to
$\Delta(-1)$.

For $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_3$ take $\lambda=-2\rho$, $J=\{s_1\}$ and the dot-antidominant
$\mu$ with $\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$; then $W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$ and by
[[thm-singular-category-o-multiplicities-are-parabolic-kl-polynomials]] the
composition and Verma-flag matrices of the singular block are
$$[M(y\cdot\mu):L(w\cdot\mu)]=(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$$
in the row/column order $(1,\,s_2,\,s_1s_2)$: explicitly $M(\mu)$ is
irreducible, $M(s_2\cdot\mu)$ has composition factors $L(\mu),L(s_2\cdot\mu)$
once each, and $M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has all three simples once; dually
$(P(\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))=1$ for all three $y$,
$(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_2\cdot\mu))=(P(s_2\cdot\mu):\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu))=1$,
with its $\Delta(\mu)$ multiplicity zero, and
$P(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\Delta(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)$ has the single top-label standard.
The surviving
simple labels are exactly the minimal coset representatives, so translation
onto the wall kills $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ for $w\notin W^J$ (for instance
$L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ in the $\mathfrak{sl}_3$ case).
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct: evaluate the wall-translation theorem on the two smallest wall data and read the matrices off the regular Kazhdan-Lusztig values at one.

1.1 **The sl_2 singular block.** For $\mu=-1=-\rho$ the dot orbit is $\{-1\}$, so $\mathcal O_{-1}$ has the single simple $L(-1)$, and by [F2] $M(-1)=L(-1)=P(-1)=\nabla(-1)$ is projective and injective. [F2, algebra]

1.2 **The sl_2 translation.** Here $W^J=\{1\}$. By [F1], $TM(-2)=M(-1)$ and $TM(0)=M(-1)$; and on simples $TL(-2)=L(-1)$, while $TL(0)=0$ because $s\notin W^J$. [F1, algebra]

1.3 **The sl_3 matrices.** For $y=(1,s_2,s_1s_2)$ the products $yw_0=(w_0,s_1s_2,s_2)$ form the descending Bruhat chain $w_0>s_1s_2>s_2$ by reduced subwords. Their supported length gaps are zero, one or two. Thus [F3] gives the displayed LOWER unitriangular matrix $A$: its row $y$, column $w$ is one exactly when $y\ge w$. BGG [F4] gives the same entries for $(P(w\cdot\mu):\Delta(y\cdot\mu))$. Thus the column at $w=1$ consists of three ones, the column at $w=s_2$ has zeros at $y=1$ and ones at $y=s_2,s_1s_2$, and the column at $w=s_1s_2$ has only the diagonal one. These are precisely the corrected projective flags displayed above; reading rows gives the unchanged simple composition factors of the three Vermas. [F3, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 **The sl_2 projective.** The relations in [F4] give $e f^kv_l=k(l-k+1)f^{k-1}v_l$ by induction using $[e,f]=h$ and $[h,f]=-2f$. For $l=0$, the span of $f^kv_0$, $k\ge1$, is the copy of $M(-2)$ generated by $fv_0$, and the quotient is the one-dimensional $L(0)$. Since $M(-2)$ is simple, BGG [F4] gives $(P(-2):\Delta(-2))=(P(-2):\Delta(0))=1$; the rank-one dot orbit has no further labels. Applying exact $T$ to this Verma flag gives two factors $\Delta(-1)=P(-1)$ by [F1] and step 1.1. Every extension of these projectives splits, so $TP(-2)\cong P(-1)\oplus P(-1)$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 **Surviving labels.** Applying [F1] to the simple labels: $L(w\cdot\lambda)$ survives translation iff $w\in W^J=\{1,s_2,s_1s_2\}$; hence $L(s_1\cdot\lambda)$ and $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(s_1s_2s_1\cdot\lambda)$ are sent to zero, as are all other non-minimal labels. This proves every displayed assertion. [F1, step 1.3, algebra] ∎

items.title: A small parabolic category O character formula
items.statement:
For $\mathfrak{sl}_3$, $\lambda=0$, $J=\{s_1\}$, the genuine regular parabolic
category has minimal-left labels $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$, with highest weights
$0,-\alpha_2,-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2$. Its generalized-standard/simple matrix is
$$N=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad N^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&1\\0&1&-1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus
$$\operatorname{ch}L(0)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(0)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)+\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2),$$
$\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_2)-\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$,
and $\operatorname{ch}L(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)=\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2)$.

For comparison retain the singular antidominant block with
$\mu+\rho=-\omega_2$ and right-minimal labels $(e,s_2,s_1s_2)$: its
composition matrix $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$ has
inverse
$\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, giving
$\operatorname{ch}L(\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(\mu)$,
and
$\operatorname{ch}L(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)=\operatorname{ch}M(s_1s_2\cdot\mu)-\operatorname{ch}M(s_2\cdot\mu)$.
The latter coefficients are Mobius values in this all-one singular chain only.
The two blocks exemplify distinct spherical and antispherical formulas; the
singular example is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the
parabolic category.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct finite matrix inversion in the two blocks, with the two products checked entrywise.

1.1 **The parabolic matrix.** By [F2] the matrix $N=(n_{y,x}(1))$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$ is the displayed upper unitriangular matrix. The displayed matrix $N^{-1}$ is its inverse: $N N^{-1}$ has entries $\sum_z n_{y,z}(1)(N^{-1})_{z,x}$, which equal $1$ for $y=x$ and $0$ otherwise (the only nonzero contributions are from $z\in\{y,\ldots,x\}$ with the alternating coefficients), and similarly $N^{-1}N=I$. Both products are finite integer calculations. [F2, algebra]

1.2 **The singular matrix.** By [F3] the composition matrix in the order $(e,s_2,s_1s_2)$ is $A=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\1&1&0\\1&1&1\end{pmatrix}$ (entry $(y,w)$ is $1$ exactly when $y\ge w$). The displayed matrix $B=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-1&1&0\\0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}$ satisfies $AB=I=BA$ by the same finite chain computation, so $A^{-1}=B$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 **The parabolic characters.** By [F1] and step 1.1, $\operatorname{ch}L(x\cdot\lambda)=\sum_y(N^{-1})_{x,y}\operatorname{ch}\Delta^J(y\cdot\lambda)$. Reading the rows of $N^{-1}$ in the order $(e,s_2,s_2s_1)$ gives exactly the three displayed character identities, using $0$, $-\alpha_2$, $-\alpha_1-2\alpha_2$ as the labels of $e\cdot0$, $s_2\cdot0$, $s_2s_1\cdot0$ by [F5]: with $\rho=\alpha_1+\alpha_2$, the type-$A_2$ reflection relations give $s_2\rho=\alpha_1$ and $s_2s_1\rho=-\alpha_2$, hence the stated dot translates after subtracting $\rho$. [F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The singular characters and the comparison.** By [F3] and [F4], $\operatorname{ch}L(w\cdot\mu)=\sum_y(A^{-1})_{w,y}\operatorname{ch}M(y\cdot\mu)$; the rows of $B=A^{-1}$ give the three displayed singular identities, in which the nonzero off-diagonal coefficients are the Mobius values $\pm1$ of this all-one chain only. The parabolic coefficients of step 2.1 include the value $+1$ in the $(1,3)$ position of $N^{-1}$, which the singular inverse does not have: the two formulas are different character formulas for different blocks, and the singular one is not the generalized-Verma character formula of the parabolic category. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎
